description: Computer-assisted proofs using interval arithmetic can rigorously certify lower bounds for B_u. By enclosing Taylor coefficients in certified intervals and verifying univalence + covering via validated numerics, one can produce machine-checkable proofs.
mathematical_formalization: Let f_N(z) = z + Σ [a_k^-, a_k^+] z^k. Verify: (1) Univalence via interval Grunsky norm. (2) Covering via interval winding number. Both hold ⟹ B_u ≥ R rigorously.
implementation_hypothesis: Use Julia IntervalArithmetic.jl or INTLAB. Represent candidate extremal function with interval coefficients. Verify Grunsky inequality and covering at target R.
experiment_seed: Take Skinner's extremal candidate. Represent first 50 Taylor coefficients as intervals. Verify univalence and covering at R=0.5709.
